full_judgment: 8. This would be evident from the Rules. Rule 10(3) provides that every nomination paper for election of a Chairman shall be made in Form A and shall be signed by the candidate and seconder. It shall be acknowledged by a Treasury Chalan or bank receipt showing deposit of the amount. Under the said Rules a certificate is to be signed by the candidate that he has consented to his nomination paper and that he is not subject to any disqualification as under sub-section (2) of section 10 of the Ordinance from being elected as Chairman or Commissioner as the case may be. Form A is appended to the Rule in schedule I. In item 12 it directs the putting of the signature or the thumb impression of the seconder with date and there is the requirement of putting the thumb impression with date arid there is a further condition to the effect that the candidate should declare under his own signature in the very nomination paper for it to be submitted on the date of submission, to the effect that he has consented to the nomination and declares that he is not disqualified for election as Chairman under the law for the time being in force. The law therefore, as provided in the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 read with the Pourashava Election Rules is very clear and it is that the nomination paper should be in Form A. It should be signed by the proposer and the seconder and it should certify that the candidate is not a disqualified person from being elected under the law for the time being in force and that he is not subject to any disqualification as under sub-section (2) or section 10 of the Ordinance from being elected as Chairman. This sub-section (2) of section 10 of the Ordinance relates to a person who is a defaulter in payment of loan. This need be certified and need be so declared on the date the nomination paper is submitted, stating the fact as to whether he is a defaulter on the date of submission of the nomination paper and not a declaration of his position on the day of scrutiny, which is one day after the submission of the nomination paper. The petitioner must clear this threshold difficulty on the day he files the nomination paper and not clear it on the day of scrutiny. Not only this status of a defaulter as to loan need be related to the day of submission of nomination paper but also to the limitation as to the age of 25 years, undischarged insolvency, limitation, citizenship limitation, etc. as it stood on the day the nomination paper is signed and submitted though it is scrutinized subsequently. This, clearly spelt out in the law and the Rules made thereunder and in proforma Form A of the Rules.
